context_spans.label: definition-algebraic-closure: an algebraic closure of F is a field extension of F that is algebraic over F and algebraically closed

standard_prerequisites: Context span 1169-1177: definition of algebraic closure (algebraic + algebraically closed)

Same chapter: lemma-size-algebraic-extension (cardinality of an algebraic extension of F is at most max(aleph_0, |F|)), lemma-algebraically-closed (equivalent characterizations, so not algebraically closed means an irreducible polynomial of degree > 1 exists), lemma-finite-is-algebraic and lemma-algebraic-permanence (algebraicity is stable in towers)
core_obligations: Consider the set I of triples (E, sigma_E, mu_E) with F subset E subset S carrying a field extension structure of F with E/F algebraic, ordered by extension of structures; a totally ordered subset has the union as upper bound, so Zorn gives a maximal element (E, sigma_E, mu_E)

If E were not algebraically closed, there is an irreducible P over E of degree > 1; then E' = E[x]/(P) is a nontrivial finite, hence algebraic, extension of E and E'/F is algebraic by algebraic permanence

Since |E'| <= max(aleph_0, |F|) < |S|, an elementary set-theoretic transport realizes E' as an element of I strictly above (E, sigma_E, mu_E), contradicting maximality; hence E is an algebraic closure of F
proof_roadmap: Set up the cardinality bound and the Zorn poset of algebraic extension structures inside the large set S
Take the maximal element and reduce to showing E is algebraically closed
Derive the contradiction by adjoining a root of an irreducible polynomial of degree > 1 and transporting the structure into S
